output.title: Anonymise first, automate second
output.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, decide one thing first: will any document that enters the process still contain customer identifiers? If yes, do not feed that file into AI yet. Mask names, amounts, addresses, and other identifying fields first, then test the workflow on the cleaned sample. That is a control step, not an AI feature, and it belongs upstream of the build.

For a small business owner, the useful check is simple. Pick one recurring workflow you already handle in email, CRM, shared drive, or a Zapier/Make step. Trace where the document first leaves your control and where human review still happens. If the path already depends on identifiable data, keep the human review and anonymise a sample before you automate anything. If the workflow can be run on a non-identifying version of the document, you have a safer test set.

This is not legal advice, and it does not remove compliance obligations. It just lowers the exposure before you ask software to do the repetitive part. A clean sample usually makes the next decision less noisy, which is the point. The owner still decides whether the workflow is worth automating at all.

A practical next step: take one real template—quote, invoice, contract, or case note—and ask, “What must be masked before I let a tool see this?”
